Further along the same surface, a dormouse sleeps curled in a bark fork behind, chin on paws, entirely undisturbed, one drop of honey resting on its ear like a bead.
Back at the rim, two long-limbed women in ember-orange and teal argue whose turn it is, both pointing at each other with full-arm conviction, their moss-velvet wings flared wide.
Out on the branch behind, a squirrel sits with both paws pressed together, watching, perfectly motionless, plainly calculating whether the reward justifies the risk of all those opponents.
Further off along the bark, one slender man in quilted indigo lies flat on his back, a full honeycomb slab across his chest, amber wings spread underneath him, finished entirely.
Down in the gap below, three of them haul on a grass-cord line, only heads and narrow shoulders visible above the rim, all leaning back, the last one seated firmly on the job.
Out on the branch behind, a woodpecker watches the whole operation with its head cocked sideways, one eye forward, the expression of a professional assessing amateur technique from a distance.
Back at the rim further off, one long-legged woman in plum lichen-scale coat stands wrapped to the eyes in oiled leaf-cloth, getting stung anyway, both fists balled at her sides.
Further along the wood, a man the size of a mouse in russet felted-down climbs with a smouldering moss bundle lashed to a twig clenched in his teeth, smoke trailing behind him.
Already on the way down the bark behind, one woman in cream moth-wing panels descends with a brimming acorn cup balanced on her head, both long arms stretched level for balance.
Out on the far side of the branch, an owl sits with both eyes shut, head pulled down into its feathers, refusing absolutely to acknowledge any of what is happening beside it.
Back at the rim, a beetle the length of a grown fae's forearm sits in a puddle of spilled honey, its amber carapace glossed gold, entirely stuck and visibly content about it.
Further off on the same surface, two narrow-shouldered men in overlapping teal bark-cloth share a sealed honeycomb slab between themselves, backs turned to the rest, contributing nothing at all.
Down below the rim, one long-limbed woman in indigo and russet has climbed higher than she needed to, purely to be higher, perching on a knot above all the others, wings fanned.
Further along the limb, a line of four in amber and moss-green all lean out over the edge at once, the last one gripping the cape of the one before, all looking straight down.
Back on the bark behind, one man in gold-stitched felted birch stands rigid with a broad sycamore leaf held up as a full-body shield, not yet having moved a single step forward.
Out on the branch behind and smaller, a snail crosses the footing at its own considered pace, carrying a bright bead of honey on its shell like a jewel it found and kept.
Further off along the rim, one narrow woman in ember-orange and cream has both boots stuck fast in a spill of honey and is lifting each foot slowly, the expression resigned entirely.
Already past the rim further back, a man in plum quilted moss-velvet descends backward down the bark, a half nutshell held against his chest with one arm, the other hand gripping a root.
Further along the same surface, two women in teal and russet lichen-scale have unrolled a folded leaf between them into a carrying sling and stand arguing about which direction to pull it.
Back at the rim, one slender man in indigo and cream simply leans out as far as he can over empty air, leaf-cloth wings catching, peering straight down with enormous calm interest.
Out on the limb behind, a moth rests with wings laid open flat, pale-furred, measuring the width of the branch with its antennae, entirely indifferent to the crisis happening beside it.
Further off on the bark behind, one woman in layered amber moth-wing sits with a grass-cord line wrapped three times round her waist, braced against a twig, being used as an anchor.
Back at the rim, one long-legged man in moss-green and plum holds a second man's ankles while that second man leans completely horizontal over the edge, arms reaching, wings held useless above him.
Further along the same surface, a man the size of a mouse in russet and gold has one foot on a bark ridge and the other on a root and has plainly committed to neither.
Already on the way down, one woman in ember-orange felted-down is descending a grass-cord line hand over hand, a sealed honeycomb slab strapped across her back, wings pressed flat under the load.
